scope: Kayenta Obsession second-edition base/core, standard 16-round, 2–4-player multiplayer, base objective deck; marked expansions, optional variants and alternate modes excluded.
summary: No definite core-flow, component-destination, cost, timing, or victory-condition error found. One objective-scoring statement resolves an ambiguity more confidently than the supplied authoritative sources support.

reviewed_sources.coverage: Core setup pp.6–12; core play pp.16–30; base gentry/improvements/market/objectives pp.35–42; base-relevant FAQ pp.76–79; base family and guest entries pp.80,83–85; all unmarked base tile entries pp.86–104; VP cards p.105; all Base-labelled objective entries pp.106–111; quick reference p.118; appended Corrigendum pp.1–2.
PDF p.12 Alderley Hall board image inspected for exact round events; PDF p.111 objective-card images and extracted page text inspected for reputation-objective ambiguity.
Both PDF pages extracted and read; only the default seasonal-market-refresh player-aid correction applies to this scope.

findings.claim: The reputation objective scores at maximum level (7), regardless of wheel position.

source_references.detail: The Base-labelled 7-VP objective says that maximum reputation is needed; it does not expressly say maximum level or that wheel position is irrelevant. Its pictured card likewise says Maximum reputation required, while illustrating the Max counter.
Defines maximum attainable reputation in standard play as level 7, position 5.
Explicitly ignores wheel position for ordinary Reputation VP and labels level 7 as Max, but does not explicitly extend that exception to the separate objective.

findings.explanation: Level-only scoring is a plausible reading, especially because the objective illustrates the Max counter. However, the objective text plus the explicit 7.5 definition also permits a literal maximum-position reading. The supplied rules and corrigendum do not expressly resolve this distinction. The summary should not present its level-only interpretation as an unqualified sourced ruling.
findings.impact: Potentially changes whether this single objective awards 7 VP to a player ending at 7.1–7.4; no definite incorrect ruling is asserted by this audit.
findings.recommended_change: Retain the source wording, 7 VP for maximum reputation, and flag the level-versus-position ambiguity unless a further authoritative clarification is obtained. Do not silently replace the claim with a new assertion that 7.5 is required.

checked_claims.claim: Twelve ordinary turns, four courtship events, no service rotation/monument income/Servants’ Hall during courtship.
Family selection begins left of random first player; reputation setup and family bonuses.
Five starting servants, five starting tiles, four family cards (five Asquith), two starter guests with leftovers returned to casual deck, five objectives.
Hire supply quantities and underbutler restrictions; unused servants excluded.
Select players plus one double-sided monuments, at most one Estate monument; activity-to-monument tiles always enter bag.
Initial six distinct market tiles: PR3 or lower, no Servants’ Hall or double-sided monuments; duplicate stacks and side/sort rules.
Exact ordinary-round events and positions: Village Fair 3/9, objectives 6, Builders’ Holiday 11, National Holiday 14, courtships 4/8/12/16.
Host step order, single-space service rotation, exact gentry counts/types, complete service, mandatory positive favours before negatives, buy and cleanup.
Pass fully refreshes service and returns discard before events/ongoing effects; choose £200 or market refresh then optional purchase; base excludes hiring on pass.
Reputation screening fixed at end of step 2; later expenditure may lower actual reputation without invalidating activity; PR restricts play, not acquisition/scoring.
Minimum 1.1, maximum 7.5, action costs 2/3/4; only special refresh limited once per turn; special actions can interrupt a reputation favour.
Negative money must be paid, may use activity earnings/VP/borrowing, cannot play if unpayable; negatives cannot precede positives.
Housekeeper and Brushing Room substitutions require none of corresponding servants available; underbutler freely substitutes base male servants.
Butler’s Room hires up to two common servants to Expended; upgraded room can recruit one common servant from any opponent-board location; Butler’s Pantry immediately grants Expended underbutler.
Servants’ Quarters tile grants one additional Quarters servant per turn; unique servants cannot be recruited or leave employ.
Guest invite visibility, screening rejection destination/visibility, optional dismissal from hand/activity/discard, family immunity, unsavoury definition.
Base family favours/VP, Fairchild service/favours/VP, base gossip penalties.
Mandatory first-use upgrades, ongoing-only restrictions, hybrid alternating categories, monument next-turn income and one-use conversion suites.
Barn triggers on hosted Estate activities; Servants’ Hall consumes a servant; Private Study rewards only upgraded Village Fair; Main Library adds objective before upgrade and VP card after.
Suite counts/service/doubling and guest destinations; South Lawn Estate family minimum; base West Terrace remains an activity.
One normal tile purchase from Market or Reserve; price modifiers and £100 minimum; no duplicates by any means; reserve schedule and Largest Wine Cellar exclusion.
Refill slides old tiles, stacks duplicates, routes Reserve tiles and sorts only new tiles; refresh withholds removed tiles until all six spaces filled.
Builders’ Holiday/Market Purchase permit multiple purchases from a single unslid market and Reserve, before a joint refill; no refresh after first Holiday purchase.
Full market refresh after each first-three courtships is the chosen standard, not merely an optional older variant.

source_ambiguities.assessment: Flagged in OBS-SOURCE-01; pictured Max counter supports level-only interpretation, but text does not explicitly waive position and maximum is defined as 7.5 elsewhere.

The final-courtship paragraph explicitly changes scoring and adds a reputation-level tiebreaker without restating VP-card awards for a persistent tie. Applying the general p.22 courtship-tie rule to players still tied after p.23’s tiebreaker is a reasonable combined reading; not treated as a summary defect.
Some pp.77–78 FAQ answers assume hiring on pass without repeating expansion labels. The explicit pp.21 and30 scope instructions identify this as expansion/optional; summary correctly excludes it.
